title: Output-weighted IO pricing pilot tied to enterprise security questionnaire minimums
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Run a controlled pilot that bills input (ingress) tokens and output (egress/streaming) tokens with asymmetric rates where output tokens are priced at a premium relative to input. Tie an optional minimum monthly commitment (floor) to enterprise customers who complete an enhanced security questionnaire and require dedicated encryption/KMS and audit logging. The pilot evaluates revenue, unit economics, perceived fairness, and procurement friction introduced by a security-tied minimum.

Hypothesis: Charging a higher rate for output tokens (and modestly discounted streaming rates for long-lived connections) will better align pricing with our server-side compute costs and reduce abusive low-output usage patterns. Tying a minimum commitment to enterprise security questionnaire completion will offset the onboarding and compliance costs (KMS/HSM, audit retention) and will be acceptable to larger customers who need these controls.

Key metrics: net revenue per active org, average tokens per request (in/out), cost per token (inferred), customer conversion rate from trial to commit, churn within first 90 days, number of security questionnaires completed, time-to-contract for enterprise deals, number of requests that hit fallback/billing errors.

Target cohorts: 1) New signups in US & EMEA on hosted API flagged as "enterprise intent" (self-reported or triggered by SSO/org-size). 2) Existing enterprise customers on trial who have raised security/compliance questions. 3) Control group: matched customers continuing on current symmetric token pricing.

Pilot parameters: - Input token rate = baseline (x) - Output token rate = 1.4x - Streaming long-tail discount for tokens after 4k tokens in a single streaming session = 0.85x output rate - Minimum monthly commitment (optional opt-in) for enterprise-SQ customers = $5k/month credit offset with 3-month grace on overage billing - Grace period for billing disputes: 14 days

Rollout plan: Week 0: finalize legal language, billing UI changes, and telemetry events. Week 1: enable for 5% of new enterprise-intent signups; instrument dashboards. Week 2-4: expand to 25% and collect early signals. Week 5-8: cohort analysis and revise pricing bands; finalize recommendation to expand or rollback.

Telemetry & instrumentation: Add events: pricing_plan_assigned, tokens_charged_io_split (with input/output counts), streaming_session_id, sq_form_completed, commit_signed. Dashboards: per-org revenue, per-request latency delta, errors due to billing logic. Ensure token-level logs respect PII/data retention policy.

Success criteria: >10% increase in net revenue per enterprise-org without >8% increase in enterprise churn; median time-to-contract does not increase by more than 14 days for customers who opt into the SQ minimum.

Risks & mitigations: - Perception of "double-charging" for long prompts: include clear billing examples in the Console and in the signup flow. - Legal pushback on minimums: provide opt-out flow and a clear SLA for dedicated security features. - Implementation complexity (billing + streaming meters): start with server-side metering flag and fallback to conservative counts for first 2 weeks.

Dependencies: ENG-40211 (billing-metering-refactor), ENG-40500 (streaming-session-tracking), PM-31670 (enterprise-sq-onboarding-scope).
